script.title: Where your files really go when you press delete
sentences: When you delete a file, it usually isn't gone.
Your computer mostly erases the label that says where the file lives.
The actual data stays on the drive, marked as space that can be reused.
Until something new is written on top, recovery tools can often bring it back.
That's how investigators rescue photos from old memory cards.
Modern solid state drives can clean up deleted blocks on their own, so recovery is harder there.
To truly wipe a device, use its full reset or encryption before you sell it.
Did you know your old phone might still remember?

script.title: Why a humanoid shape is not proof of human intelligence
sentences: If a robot looks human, should you assume it understands the world like a human?
A humanoid body is an engineering design that can help machines interact with environments built for people.
Its appearance alone tells you little about how its software reasons, learns, or handles unexpected events.
A system can perform an impressive learned behavior while remaining unreliable on tasks that seem easier to us.
You need to know the operating conditions, degree of autonomy, and whether a person is helping remotely.
Safety also depends on physical forces and failure handling, not simply how friendly the face looks.
Judge the demonstrated capability and its limits separately from the emotional impression created by the robot’s shape.
Would a human-looking face make you trust a robot more or less?
